main_body: Small farm hut: a large tiled roof slope (rows 1-21), a log wall front with a dark doorway and a recessed window (rows 24-34), and a wooden porch/bench on legs in front (rows 35-43)
top_band: Roof slope, orange/maroon tile pattern with a light highlight row at rows 3-7, running to rows 3-21. It is separated from the wall by a dark eave row at rows 22-23 (L=23). A ridge line sits above it at rows 1-2.
evidence: The roof is a big sloped surface with tile rows and a distinct dark eave shadow at rows 22-23 above the log wall. It reads like the stall roof in the reference, as a lighter horizontal mass sitting above the front face. The wall below has its own shading, an inset dark doorway and an inset window frame. The front porch plank (rows 35-37) is a horizontal top surface with legs below it, and it is separated from the wall. The roof has no hips or gables, but both a top surface and a front face are clearly drawn, so it does not read as a flat elevation.

style.evidence: Median 37 colours per tile against 18 and 11 for the references, 61 distinct colours in total, and 0% flat-fill coverage. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean brown or maroon beside the wood and roof. The roof has a per-tile highlight, light, mid and dark pattern, and the log wall has grain bands in several browns. It sits at or above the references on every measured fact. The piece is small, but it is not thinner or more sticker-like than the references.
